 The Travel Beauty and Skincare Essentials Our Editors Pack in Their Carry-Ons 
 The skincare, makeup, and haircare essentials they swear by for every trip.
 By Josiah Soto Published: Nov 16, 2026 4:39 PM EST Save Article Share Article We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we back. Why Trust Us? 
 3 min read Cleansers 
 Toners 
 Serums 
 Moisturizers 
 Sunscreens 
 Makeup Essentials 
 Hair Essentials 
 Packing for a trip is stressful enough without having to decide which skincare and beauty products deserve a spot in your bag. And if you've ever stepped off a plane with skin that feels tight, dry, or just a little off, you know how much travel can throw off your regular routine.
 Between dry airplane cabins, climate changes, and long days spent getting from one place to another, your skin can go through a lot when you're traveling. That's why I like to pack products that focus on hydration, support my skin barrier, and, of course, provide sun protection. I also try to stick to formulas that I already know work for my skin rather than experimenting with anything new while I'm away.
 I'm not the only one who's particular about what makes it into my toiletry bag. Prevention's senior commerce editor, Charlotte Lewis Finigan, also has a handful of skincare, makeup, and haircare essentials she swears by, including a few travel-size products that have earned permanent spots in her routine.
 Below, we're sharing the travel beauty essentials we actually use and love, from affordable drugstore cleansers to splurge-worthy serums. And while some come in convenient mini sizes, others are compact enough to bring along without sacrificing the products we already use at home.
 Cleansers
 A good cleanser is one of the first things I pack when traveling. After a long day of wearing sunscreen, makeup, or just being out and about, I want something that can remove everything without leaving my skin feeling stripped. And when you're already dealing with dry airplane air or a different climate, keeping your cleansing routine gentle is especially important.
 A Necessary First Step Bioderma Bioderma - Sensibio Micellar Water
 $7 at Amazon I never travel without micellar water, and Bioderma's Sensibio H2O is easily one of my favorites. I primarily use it as the first step in my nighttime routine to remove sunscreen, but plenty of my friends swear by it for taking off makeup, too. It's gentle, doesn't leave my skin feeling tight, and the 3.33-ounce bottle is perfect for tossing into a carry-on.
 A Hydrating Cleanser Kiehl's Ultra Facial Barrier Hydrating Cleanser
 $19 at Amazon After going in with my Bioderma micellar water, I follow up with this cleanser from Kiehl's. The cream-to-foam formula is incredibly gentle on my skin but still leaves my face feeling clean, without that dry, squeaky feeling I try to avoid. I especially appreciate it when traveling because I don't want to deal with irritation or dryness from switching to a harsher cleanser. Plus, the mini is just 2.5 ounces.
 Cult Favorite CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser
 $17 at Ulta Beauty Credit: Cerave Charlotte's approach to travel skincare is pretty simple: Stick to what works. Because her skin tends to be sensitive, she always packs her regular CeraVe Hydrating Facial Cleanser rather than taking her chances with whatever soap is waiting at the hotel. The formula contains ceramides, glycerin, and hyaluronic acid to cleanse without stripping away moisture. Her money-saving tip? She buys the larger size for home and refills her travel bottle instead of buying a new mini every time she goes away.
 Toners
 I love using a hydrating toner after cleansing, especially when I'm traveling. It's an easy way to add another layer of moisture before applying serums and creams, and I find that it helps my skin feel more comfortable when it's particularly dehydrated. Rather than packing exfoliating toners, I'd stick with gentle, moisturizing formulas that focus on hydration.
 So Milky innisfree Green Tea Ceramide Milk Barrier Essence
 $15 at Amazon This Korean milky toner is a great option for anyone who wants extra hydration without adding another heavy cream to their routine. It combines green tea, ceramides, and hyaluronic acid to help keep skin feeling soft and moisturized, with a lightweight texture that layers nicely underneath serums. I also love that the mini comes in a 3-ounce bottle, so you're getting a generous amount of product without exceeding the carry-on liquid limit.
 For Dewy Skin Laneige Mini Cream Skin Toner
 $16 at Amazon Another hydrating option worth considering is Laneige's Cream Skin, which almost feels like a toner and lightweight moisturizer in one. The milky formula uses ceramides and peptides to help support the skin's moisture barrier, making it particularly appealing for dry or dehydrated skin. The 1.69-ounce mini is convenient for traveling, and its nourishing texture makes it an easy addition to a pared-down skincare routine.
 Internet Favorite Rhode Mini Glazing Milk Ceramide Facial Essence
 $20 at Sephora Hailey Bieber's rhode Glazing Milk is a great addition to any travel skincare routine, especially when your skin needs a little extra hydration. The milky essence is packed with three types of ceramides, beta-glucan, and glycerin to help strengthen the skin's moisture barrier, soothe dryness, and leave your complexion looking dewy and refreshed. It's lightweight enough to layer underneath your favorite serums and moisturizers, making it an easy way to give your skin some extra love after a long flight. Plus, the 1.7-ounce mini is perfect for tossing into your carry-on.
 Serums
 If there's one skincare category I refuse to skip when traveling, it's serums. I love how much hydration you can get from just a few drops, especially when your skin starts feeling dehydrated after a flight. My favorites focus on keeping skin plump, comfortable, and hydrated rather than loading up on strong active ingredients.
 Serums 
 My Holy Grail Iunik Beta-Glucan Power Moisture Serum
 $19 at Amazon This is one of my all-time favorite hydrating serums, and it's a product I constantly find myself coming back to. The Korean formula uses beta-glucan to attract and retain moisture, leaving my skin feeling incredibly hydrated and looking noticeably plumper. I especially love how lightweight it feels, even when I'm layering it underneath a richer moisturizer. If you're looking for a straightforward hydrating serum that doesn't make your routine complicated, this is a great one.
 A Luxury Pick Epicutis Lipid Serum
 $250 at ohbeauty.com If you're willing to splurge on your travel skincare, Epicutis Lipid Serum is a luxury option worth knowing about. The formula contains just eight ingredients, including hyaluronic acid and the brand's proprietary TSC ingredient, which is designed to help calm visible redness and irritation. It's an appealing choice for skin that feels stressed, dehydrated, or uncomfortable after traveling. It's definitely an investment, but the lightweight texture and focus on soothing skin make it a particularly interesting pick for sensitive-skin routines.
 Deeply Hydrates Experiment Super Saturated Ultra Hydrating Barrier Serum
 $28 at Amazon Experiment Beauty's Super Saturated Serum is all about hydration, which is exactly what I want when traveling. Its formula contains a whopping 30% glycerin, along with polyglutamic acid, to help draw moisture into the skin and give it a bouncy, plumped-up appearance. The juicy texture makes it a great option for layering underneath moisturizer, particularly when your skin is feeling extra thirsty. It's also a nice alternative to some of the more expensive hydrating serums out there.
 Moisturizers
 Whether you're flying somewhere warm and sunny or heading into colder weather, a good moisturizer is essential. I tend to prioritize formulas that support my skin barrier and keep my face comfortable throughout the day. Charlotte, meanwhile, loves having a richer nighttime moisturizer on hand, particularly because her skin gets noticeably drier when she travels.
 For Inflamed Skin Dieux Skin Mercy Recovery Cream
 $38 at dieuxskin.com Credit: Dieux When my skin is feeling irritated or needs a little extra care, Dieux's Skin Mercy Recovery Cream is one of the products I reach for. It's formulated with 1% colloidal oatmeal, a skin-protecting ingredient that helps soothe itching and irritation, along with glycerin to provide hydration. I particularly like this type of moisturizer for traveling because it focuses on keeping skin calm and comfortable rather than introducing a bunch of harsh actives. It's a great option to have on hand when your skin isn't cooperating.
 Great for Winter KraveBeauty Mochi Berrier Moisture Cream
 $32 at Amazon I've become a big fan of KraveBeauty's Mochi Berrier Moisture Cream, particularly as the weather gets colder. It's richer than the brand's Oat So Simple Water Cream, making it a great option when I'm traveling somewhere chilly or dealing with especially dry skin. Despite its thick, bouncy texture, I find that it doesn't leave my face feeling overly greasy, and it's been comfortable on my acne-prone skin. I especially love using it at night when I want to wake up with skin that feels soft and moisturized.
 Deeply Moisturizing Ole Henriksen Skin Barrier Strengthening Moisturizer
 $20 at Sephora Charlotte calls this moisturizer her holy grail for nighttime, especially when traveling leaves her skin feeling drier than usual. Between not drinking enough water, the dry air on planes, and adjusting to different climates, she finds that her skin needs a little extra nourishment while she's away. This cream combines peptides, ceramides, and hyaluronic acid in a rich formula that still sinks into skin surprisingly quickly. And unlike a bulky jar of face cream, the 0.5-ounce mini barely takes up any space in a toiletry bag.

 No matter where I'm headed, sunscreen always makes the cut. Whether you're sightseeing, spending time outdoors, or just walking around a new city, daily SPF is essential for protecting skin from UV damage. Luckily, plenty of lightweight formulas feel good enough to wear every day, including some that work beautifully under makeup.
 My Favorite Sunscreen KraveBeauty Beet The Sun SPF 40
 $20 at Amazon Credit: KraveBeauty If you know me, you know how much I love KraveBeauty's Beet The Sun. It's easily one of my favorite sunscreens, largely because of how lightweight and comfortable it feels on my skin. The SPF 40 formula provides broad-spectrum protection without leaving a white cast or that greasy finish that can make some sunscreens unpleasant to wear. It's one of those products I genuinely look forward to applying, which makes remembering to use SPF every day a whole lot easier.
 For Glowing Skin Sofie Pavitt Face Screentime Non-Comedogenic Hydrating Sunscreen
 $38 at Sephora For acne-prone skin, Sofie Pavitt Face's Screentime is another sunscreen worth packing. Developed with breakout-prone skin in mind, this broad-spectrum SPF 30 combines sun protection with hydrating ingredients like ectoin, niacinamide, and vitamin E. The formula is designed to feel lightweight and comfortable without leaving a white cast, and it wears well underneath makeup. I particularly like the idea of bringing a sunscreen that provides some added hydration when traveling.
 Very Protective Supergoop! Unseen Sunscreen SPF 50
 $38 at Amazon Charlotte is a big fan of Supergoop!'s Unseen Sunscreen, especially because it doubles as an excellent makeup primer. The clear gel formula is incredibly lightweight, doesn't irritate her sensitive skin, and layers beautifully underneath her everyday makeup. It also provides broad-spectrum SPF 50 protection without leaving a white cast. If you're trying to streamline your morning routine while traveling, a sunscreen that also helps prep your skin for makeup is a pretty convenient addition.
 Makeup Essentials
 Even when you're trying to travel light, a few makeup products are worth making room for. Charlotte's favorites focus on looking polished without spending too much time getting ready, which is especially helpful when you're heading straight from the airport to dinner or squeezing in a full day of sightseeing.
 Tried and True Dr. Jart+ Premium BB Tinted Moisturizer
 $49 at Amazon Charlotte loves this BB cream for the way it instantly makes her look more refreshed and put together, even when she's running on very little sleep. The recently reformulated product has a creamier texture that she finds even easier to blend, leaving behind a beautiful, hydrated glow while evening out her skin tone. She's also a fan of the expanded shade range, which now includes eight flexible shades. While it isn't technically a mini, the 1.35-ounce tube is carry-on friendly and offers a convenient alternative to packing a separate foundation.
 Must Have Tarte Mini Tartelette XL Lengthening & Tubing Mascara
 $15 at Sephora Charlotte has gone through multiple tubes of this mascara, and once you hear why, it's easy to understand the appeal. Just one coat makes her lashes look noticeably longer, thicker, and more voluminous, without requiring a complicated makeup routine. But her favorite part is how easy it is to remove: The tubing formula slides off with warm water, so there's no need to spend extra time scrubbing at your lashes at the end of a long day. The miniature tube is also small enough to throw into a purse for touch-ups on the go.
 Easy Application Rhode Pocket Blush Buildable Hydrating Cream
 Shop at Sephora Pocket Blush is one of those makeup products that makes getting ready while traveling so much easier. The creamy, hydrating formula melts into the skin and blends effortlessly for a natural-looking flush of color, whether you want a subtle rosy glow or something a little more pigmented. It also doubles as a lip color, so you can get two uses out of one product without taking up extra space in your makeup bag. Plus, the compact stick is small enough to toss into your purse for quick touch-ups throughout the day, and you can apply it with just your fingers—no makeup brushes necessary.
 Hair Essentials
 Haircare is another category that's easy to overpack, especially when you're trying to bring every brush, comb, and styling product you use at home. Charlotte's solution is one compact brush that works on wet and dry hair, so you don't have to pack multiple tools.
 Curls-on-the-Go Amika Hydro Rush Intense Moisture Leave-In Conditioner
 $14 at Amazon As someone with curly hair, I always need a product that can bring my curls back to life in a pinch, especially when I'm traveling. That's where amika's Hydro Rush Leave-In Conditioner comes in. Packed with hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid, squalane, and coconut water, this lightweight spray helps moisturize dry strands, tame frizz, and make detangling a breeze. I love reaching for it when my curls need a quick refresh before heading out, without having to go through my entire styling routine. Plus, the 2-ounce mini is perfect for throwing into my carry-on, so I can keep my curls looking cute wherever I'm headed.
 The Best Detangler Tangle Teezer Ultimate Detangler Hairbrush
 $11 at Amazon Charlotte's fine hair tangles easily, so a good detangling brush is an absolute must whenever she travels. She loves Tangle Teezer's Mini Ultimate Detangler because it's gentle enough to use on wet hair but effective at smoothing out knots when her hair is dry, too. That means she doesn't have to pack multiple brushes or sacrifice precious space in her suitcase. Better yet, it's small enough to keep in her purse, making it just as useful during a long travel day as it is once she's reached her destination.
 The Best Diffuser Dyson Supersonic Travel Styling Duo
 Now 23% Off $392 $300 at Amazon If you're someone who doesn't trust hotel hair dryers to get the job done, Dyson's Supersonic Travel Styling Duo might be worth making room for in your suitcase. The travel-friendly hair dryer is 32% smaller and 25% lighter than the Supersonic Nural, but still delivers powerful airflow for quick drying without exposing hair to extreme heat. It also features universal voltage, so you can use it while traveling internationally without worrying about voltage compatibility. The set includes Dyson's Omega Leave-In Conditioning Spray to help nourish hair, reduce frizz, and make detangling easier, plus a travel bag to keep everything organized. It's definitely a splurge, but a convenient option for anyone who wants salon-worthy styling on the go.
 Josiah Soto Grooming and Style Commerce Editor Josiah Soto is a commerce editor and writer at Hearst Magazines, where he covers skincare, grooming, beauty, and style for Men’s Health , Prevention , and BestProducts.com .
